messages.content:
You are a clinical psychologist writing a psychological case vignette
grounded in Ehlers & Clark's (2000) cognitive model of PTSD.

Write a realistic clinical case vignette for a patient with PTSD.
The vignette should read as a cohesive, flowing portrait — not a structured report.
Weave together who this person is, what happened to them, how they experience their
symptoms day to day, how they cope, and what toll this takes on their life and relationships.


Do not use section headers, numbered points, or clinical labels for symptoms.
Write 200–300 words in third person.
Cover: presenting complaints, trauma background, cognitive distortions, avoidance, and maintaining factors.
Avoid excessive jargon - write for a clinical case conference audience.

Please write a clinical vignette for the following patient presenting with PTSD.
Patient demographics:
- Age: 20
- Gender: Male
- Ethnicity: South Asian
- Relationship Status: Single
- Occupation: Writer
- Trauma Type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one
- Pcl5: 72

Aryan is a 20-year-old, South Asian male who identifies as single and works as a freelance writer. He has been struggling with intense distress since the unexpected death of his younger brother, Ravi, three months ago. Aryan's world came crashing down when he received the news that Ravi had been in a fatal car accident while returning from a late-night shift at his part-time job. Aryan and Ravi were inseparable growing up; they shared a deep bond through their love for writing and exploring their cultural heritage together. Losing Ravi has left Aryan feeling lost, as if he’s missing an essential part of himself. Every day since the accident, Aryan wakes up with a heavy heart, knowing that his brother is no longer there to share in life's joys and sorrows. He often feels like he can hear Ravi calling out to him from another room, only to realize moments later that it was just his mind playing tricks on him. These intrusions are accompanied by vivid flashbacks of the phone call where he learned about the accident, leaving him feeling as if he’s reliving the moment over and over again. Aryan’s writing, once a source of comfort and creativity, has become increasingly difficult to manage. He describes sitting in front of his computer for hours without being able to put anything down on paper. His mind races with thoughts of Ravi, and he often catches himself editing old essays they worked on together or imagining how Ravi would respond to new pieces Aryan is writing. The anxiety and overwhelming sadness have also disrupted Aryan’s sleep pattern significantly. He struggles to fall asleep, plagued by nightmares where he relives the accident and wakes up drenched in sweat. Even when he manages a few hours of sleep, it's often interrupted by intrusive thoughts that leave him feeling restless and exhausted throughout the day. Aryan has become increasingly isolated since Ravi’s death. Once a social person who enjoyed attending literary gatherings and book clubs with his brother, he now avoids these events altogether. The thought of going to a place where Ravi was also present fills Aryan with an intense sense of dread and fear that triggers panic attacks. He feels like everyone around him is moving on while he’s stuck in the same painful moment. On days when Aryan can muster up some energy, he immerses himself in his brother’s possessions—books, articles, and photographs—as if holding onto them will bring Ravi back. This obsession with Ravi’s things has taken over his apartment; every surface is littered with mementos that serve as painful reminders of the past. Despite these challenges, Aryan still attends to his daily responsibilities, though he often feels disconnected from the tasks at hand. Writing assignments come in late or are submitted half-heartedly because he can’t focus on anything other than his grief and loss. His friends have noticed a change but aren’t quite sure how to support him effectively. Aryan’s life has become a series of fragmented moments, each one haunted by memories of Ravi. The weight of his brother's absence is so heavy that it feels as though he’s carrying the world on his shoulders every day. He longs for some form of relief from this constant pain and yearns to find a way to honor Ravi without being consumed by grief. Navigating each day, Aryan tries to hold onto the small moments of joy and connection, hoping they will eventually become more than fleeting glimpses through the fog of his trauma.
